item.text:
The definitions are split between [constants.ts](/app/packages/shared/lib/constants.ts:450), which defines `BASE_SIZE` and `GIGA`, and [humanSize.ts](/app/packages/shared/lib/helpers/humanSize.ts:5), which defines `sizeUnits`. The requested `helpers/size.ts` does not exist. The likely fix is to move `BASE_SIZE` and `sizeUnits` there and update the consumers to import from it.

The main behavior difference is in [MemberStorageSelector.tsx](/app/packages/components/containers/members/MemberStorageSelector.tsx:29): Drive Pro and Drive Business currently receive `1000 * GIGA`; the requested `sizeUnits.TB` is `1024 * GIGA`. Its slider step also uses `GIGA`. The member creation and editing modals, [CSV import](/app/packages/components/containers/members/multipleUserCreation/csv.ts:93), and organization setup use `GIGA` for allocations or display units. Bonus values in `constants.ts` and calendar and contacts imports also need the shared source. Inline gigabyte calculations additionally appear in referral and offer copy components; whether the requested sweep includes shared Drive constants is less clear.

Existing CSV and human size tests cover conversions, but I found no focused test for the selector’s plan defaults. I recorded the findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). Project source and tests were left untouched under this pass’s diagnosis-only instruction.
